text:
LINCOLN, Neb. (KOLN) - Car lovers gathered outside Dillard’s at Gateway Mall Saturday, turning the parking lot into a time capsule for the fourth annual Fashion on Wheels car show, an event raising money for the Autism Family Network.

Among the polished classics was Ray Cochran’s 2004 Corvette, a gift from his wife marking their 60th wedding anniversary. Cochran said the show was only the second time he’d ever brought the car out for an event.

“It’s a 2004 Corvette,” Cochran said. “It’s got slotted drilled discs on the brakes and it’s got a broiler in the exhaust system.”

Every dollar raised goes to the Autism Family Network in Lincoln, which works to provide resources and opportunities for people on the autism spectrum and their families.

“It makes it so that we can provide these events for different people,” said Melissa Blakemore with the Autism Family Network. “It’s pretty cool to see how many people come out with their cars and support us.”

Unlike judged shows, Fashion on Wheels kept it simple with no classes, no requirements, just stories under the hood.

Folks talked motors, gaskets and the details that keep decades-old cars running — all while supporting a cause that brought the community together.
